thread.title: Asian markets sink, led by Apple suppliers, on Trump's latest tariff threat

author: morningstar.com
title: Asian markets sink, led by Apple suppliers, on Trump's latest tariff threat
text:
By Dow Jones Newswire
iPhone component-makers' shares hit hard in Hong Kong, Taiwan
Asian stocks dropped Tuesday following President Donald Trump's announcement of potentially $200 billion in additional tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-seeks-additional-200-billion-in-tariffs-against-china-and-threatens-even-more-2018-06-18)against imports from China.
In Japan, the yen jumped on that news, and the Nikkei was off almost 1%. Export-related stocks slid, with Komatsu (6301.TO) shedding 1.5% while Honda (HMC) was down 0.9%. The dollar was down 0.4% versus the yen at Yen110.13.
China stocks opened sharply lower following Monday's holiday and amid increased trade tensions with the U.S. The Shanghai Composite was off 2.2% in early trading and the Shenzhen Composite was off 2%. The Shanghai benchmark has fallen three straight days and four consecutive weeks, finishing Friday at a 21-month low.
Apple Inc. (AAPL) suppliers' stocks were hit hard around the region, despite a report that U.S. tariffs would spare iPhones (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-reportedly-told-apple-that-tariffs-against-china-would-spare-iphones-2018-06-18) produced in China. IPhone-camera maker Cowell Holdings (1415.HK) skidded 10% in Hong Kong to fresh record lows, while smartphone-lens maker Sunny Optical (2382.HK) pulled back a further 4.4% and acoustics firm AAC Technologies (2018.HK) fell 2.8%. In Taiwan, Sunny peer Largan Precision (3008.TW) was off 4.2%. Apple product assembler Hon Hai Precision Industry (2317.TW) dropped 2%. Indexes in Hong Kong and Taiwan were each down more than 1%.
Meanwhile, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was up 0.5% as the Aussie dollar fell on the trade talk. Korea's benchmark dipped and New Zealand's NZX was down about 0.3%.
-Dow Jones Newswire; 18-18 2330ET
